MOCK CAMPAIGN

02 / Essence × Wicked

GOOD.
WICKED.
Beautiful.

An independent student concept. Not an official collaboration, and not affiliated with essence, Universal Pictures or the Wicked franchise.

The look

Concept visuals for the mock campaign. Not official essence or Wicked products.

Which side are you? Drag the slider

Glinda

Soft · Playful · Feminine · Glossy · Pink

Elphaba

Bold · Confident · Unapologetic · Dramatic · Green

The big idea

Good looks good on you.

Rather than choosing between "good" and "wicked", the campaign celebrates both sides of your beauty personality. Everyone has a soft, glossy day and a bold, dramatic one.

Target audience

Gen Z and young millennial beauty fans who love pop culture and playful, affordable makeup, and who share looks on TikTok and Instagram.

Objectives

  • Spark conversation around the two looks
  • Drive trial of the duo set
  • Grow user-generated content

Creative direction

Split-screen visuals: pink gloss on one side, emerald drama on the other. Duets, mirrored poses and one product shown two ways.

Social strategy

  • Which side are you? A personality-style quiz for stories
  • Good × Wicked. Two looks, one product
  • Unlock your look. Short videos turning an everyday look into a character look

Creator strategy

Pair creators as duets, one per side, with micro-creators inviting followers to pick their side and post their own.

KPIs

  • Engagement and shares
  • Number of user posts with the campaign hashtag
  • Quiz completions
  • Duo set sell-through and new customers

Campaign rollout

1. TeaseSplit-screen teasers, "good or wicked?" polls, creator mystery packages.
2. LaunchDuo set drop, creator duets, quiz goes live, product display in stores or online.
3. SustainUser content features, "unlock your look" tutorials, best-performing looks restocked.

Campaign mock-ups

essence_concept•••
Good × Wicked. Two looks. One product. Which side are you? 💚💗
Two sides, one display. Soft and glossy meets bold and dramatic.

Real-world context

A crowded space, so the idea has to be sharp

Beauty brands have been releasing Wicked-themed products since the first film. Examples include M·A·C's Elphaba and Glinda-inspired palette and lipsticks (Myer, 2024), Lush's ten-piece collection with Universal Pictures for Wicked: For Good (2025) and a Kristin Ess Hair limited edition (2025). That is why this concept focuses on personality and participation, not just green and pink packaging.

Sources: Theatre Matters (M·A·C), Cosmetics Business (Lush), Newswire (Kristin Ess Hair).
